reason: Not refuted on semantics. High byte: LDA p_hi; LSR (C=h0, A bit0=h1); EOR/AND #1/EOR p_lo (p_lo with bit0=h1); ROR; ROR (h1 h0 l7..l2); LSR; LSR = (p_hi AND 3)<<4 | p_lo>>4, the old value, bits 7-6 clear. Amplitude latch: n=v>>4 is 0-15 (sfx_v 0-&F8 by the clamps), and n EOR (bits OR &1F) = (n EOR &1F) OR bits for bits &80/&A0/&C0/&E0, so g2_att_bits (&9F,&BF,&DF,&FF) is right for tone and noise (X=3). Cache: sfx_noise_written,0-2 are written only by the request path (STA ...,X with the effect's high byte; effects are in bank 5, >= &80, never 0-15) and read only by the noise path at X=3 (grep of src and tools: no other reader or writer). sfx_n is nonzero only after a request (EQUB 0 at start, ended/sfx_silence zero it, sfx_next_ramp is reached only from the request path or a running channel), so every output on a tone channel is preceded by a request that invalidated the cache; while a channel runs nothing else writes its attenuation (no other chip writer in play: OSWORD 7 only when not irq_owned, keyboard scan uses latch line 3 and DDRA only, ended writes att 15 but zeroes sfx_n). A skipped amplitude leaves the chip's latch on the tone register, harmless because every following write is a latch byte (the only data byte is the tone high byte, always right after its latch). Exits: C and V preserved by the new sfx_write tail as by the old; the tone path's CMP changes C, but sfx_tick's next use is LDA sfx_dp / CLC on both paths. Y leaves sfx_write as 8 (was 0) and Z=0 (was 1): no caller reads either (sfx_output's caller loads A then CLC; request loop TAY; channel loop resets; sfx_silence restores P with PLP, its callers load Y (take_irq_for_play) or go through OSBYTE &13 (give_irq_back -> clear_title_screen); the irq handler PLYs). Stack balanced on every exit (g2_same RTS returns sfx_output's JSR). All runs are in the interrupt or under SEI (sfx_silence), so nothing interleaves; main code only stores sfx_request. No label+N or tool references to wait_low/wait_high/sfx_write's tail. Timing: only the 21-cycle LDY #4 wait after the write enable rises is dropped; the next fall is >= 39 cycles later on every path (noise control -> amplitude 39, tone low -> high 44, silence loop and tick paths longer), the chip needs 16. Recount (2 MHz cycles, no VIA stretch, no page crossings): each sfx_write call saves 21; a tone output saves 94 when its amplitude is unchanged (21 low write + 4 high byte arithmetic + 21 high write + 48 amplitude skipped: 25 against 73) and 58 when it changes (amplitude 61 against 73); the claim's 93 matches the unchanged case within a cycle. Bytes: 63 -> 76, +13 (the claim's -13 bytes saved), bank 5's room to be confirmed by the build's ASSERT.
